capabilities: Render force-directed node graphs from gr code blocks
Drag nodes to re-heat the physics simulation
Show node labels, colors, and hover tooltips
Adjust graph height per block with a directive
Follow the vault theme's light/dark styling
disambiguation: Not a vault-wide graph view; it renders small ad-hoc graphs (up to a few dozen nodes) written directly in code blocks.
extras: Installation is manual or via BRAT only; clicking nodes does nothing yet (click-to-open-note is a planned feature); the simulation is intentionally lightweight and limited to idea-sized graphs.
intentEvidence: Like the native graph view, but for arbitrary ideas you define on the spot, not vault links.
problem: Obsidian's graph view only shows relationships between vault notes, so there is no way to visualize small ad-hoc graphs defined on the spot inside a note.
summary: Renders interactive, force-directed node graphs inline in notes from simple gr code blocks, with draggable nodes and hover tooltips.
